subject: Encryption & data residency follow-up — Finexia PII handling
messages:
From: Lena Müller <lena.mueller@finexia.de>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T13:00:00+01:00
Subject: Follow-up: encryption & residency requirements for Finexia

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. I wanted to capture the high-level requirements we discussed and confirm a few details so our legal and platform teams can move forward with a short list of vendors. Key items from our side: 

- Data residency: all PII and transaction payloads must be stored in the EU (DE, FR or NL regions).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ required, mutual TLS preferable for service-to-service calls.
- At-rest: customer-managed keys (BYOK) is a hard requirement for production; must integrate with AWS KMS or allow HSM-backed keys.
- Key controls: customers must retain control of key lifecycle (rotate, revoke); no plaintext key export to Redwood-managed services.
- Audit logging: access logs (who/what/when) for key operations and API calls retained for 7 years; logs must not contain raw PII.
- Data retention / deletion: we need policy support for data deletion on subject request and proof of deletion for PII derived artifacts.

Open clarification points we discussed: 1) can Redwood support per-region key partitioning (one CMK per region)? 2) what is your approach to prefix/KV cache — can we enforce token redaction before cache? 3) do you offer HSM import or only KMS keys managed via API? 

Please confirm those three items and share any security docs you recommend we review. I attached our internal questionnaire; happy to walk through it with your security teams.

Best,
Lena Müller
Head of Platform Security — Finexia GmbH

Attachment: finexia-security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Lena Müller <lena.mueller@finexia.de>, Finexia Security Team <security@finexia.de>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, priy a_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T16:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: encryption & residency requirements for Finexia

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the questionnaire. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

Answers to your three clarifications:
1) Per-region CMKs: yes — Redwood Private supports per-region CMKs. For our hosted offering we can route keys to region-specific KMS instances; for Dedicated/Private deployments you can provision CMKs per region and configure routing policies.

2) Prefix/KV cache redaction: we support request-level redaction rules and can disable caching for routes that contain PII. We also offer a pre-processing hook to strip or tokenise sensitive fields before they reach the runtime cache.

3) HSM import vs KMS-only: We support both flows. Hosted customers commonly bring keys via AWS KMS with an external key policy. For higher-assurance scenarios we integrate with HSM-backed keys (PKCS#11 import or Cloud HSM) and can accept imported key material during Private deployments (import subject to HSM vendor constraints).

Attachments and links: I’ve attached our draft SLA and a short KMS options matrix for your review (attached). Our security questionnaire answers are in progress — we’ll populate your PDF and return it within 48 hours.

Proposed next steps: 
- Technical deep-dive (60m) with our security engineer to validate HSM import mechanisms and demo per-region CMK routing. Suggested times: Tue 2026-12-22 09:00–11:00 CET or Wed 2026-12-23 14:00–16:00 CET.
- Provide a short design note outlining how we perform key rotation, key ownership boundaries, and log redaction (deliverable: 2–3 page doc, due by 2026-12-28).
- Legal: share a redlined SLA + KMS clause for review.

Action owners:
- Rishi to coordinate engineering deep-dive and produce design note.
- Priya to prepare a KMS clause draft and coordinate with legal if needed.
- Evelyn to collect answers to the questionnaire and return to Lena.

Would you like us to include a brief architecture diagram that shows where keys live and how traffic routes across EU regions?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (pdf), kms-options-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Finexia Security Team <security@finexia.de>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: lena.mueller@finexia.de
Date: 2026-12-21T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: encryption & residency requirements for Finexia

Evelyn — appreciate the rapid reply. A few clarifications from the security team after reviewing your notes: 

- HSM import: we require that imported key material cannot be exported back out of the HSM under any circumstances and that Redwood cannot access raw key material. Is that enforced in your import flow?
- Key rotation: we need an option to define rotation cadence from our side (customer-triggered rotation), and an audit trail that includes both rotation events and who performed them.
- Logging: confirm logs are write-once and that PII does not appear in plain text. If any derivative (e.g., embeddings, vector store entries) contains PII, we require a deletion workflow with verifiable proof.

For the deep-dive, Tue 2026-12-22 10:00 CET works best for us. Please send a calendar invite and include your security engineer and an infra person who can speak to KV cache behavior.

Thanks,
Finexia Security Team

Folks — following Finexia’s replies, here are concrete action items before tomorrow’s deep-dive (2026-12-22 10:00 CET). Please review and flag if any timing conflicts.

1) Rishi — owner for technical deep-dive (you’ll lead). Prepare a short slide that covers:
   - HSM import flow (PKCS#11 / CloudHSM path), explicit statement that imported key material is non-exportable.
   - Per-region CMK routing architecture (diagram showing EU regions and CMK boundaries).
   - KV cache redaction: explain pre-processing hooks, optional disable of caching for PII routes, and how tokenisation/redaction integrates with runtime.
   - Audit trail examples (rotation event logs, key-use logs).

2) Priya — legal/KMS clause draft and sample redlined SLA. Add language to cover: customer-triggered rotation, proof-of-deletion for derivative artifacts, and log retention controls.

3) Evelyn — I’ll send calendar invite and a 1-page agenda + list of deliverables after the call (design note due 2026-12-28). I’ll also collate the questionnaire answers and send back to Finexia within 48 hours.

4) Ops note: we should prepare a short demo snippet showing how to disable caching for a route and a script to run a mock key rotation that generates the audit entries the customer requested.

Attachments for internal prep: I started a Drive folder with the SLA and questionnaire (link below). Please add your slides/notes to the folder by 08:00 CET tomorrow.
